title: PR 05 — Crypto core and vault recovery key
description: Ship the complete client-side cryptographic contract: PBKDF2 master key derivation, domain-separated HKDF subkeys, auth hash for server verification, random vault key with wrap/unwrap, versioned AES-256-GCM item envelope, and a recovery key that wraps the same vault key. Requirement IDs: TASK-13, TASK-14, TASK-15, TASK-16, TASK-17.
acceptanceCriteria: `masterKey` derives from the master password with PBKDF2-SHA256 at the stored iteration count (default 600000) using WebCrypto
`authHash` is derived through HKDF with info `bw-auth` and cannot be reversed to the master key
`vaultKey` is 32 random bytes from `crypto.getRandomValues` and is only ever wrapped, never stored or transmitted in plaintext
Changing the master password re-wraps the same `vaultKey`, so existing ciphertext stays decryptable
Item envelope is versioned (`v: 1`, `alg: A256GCM`) with a fresh 96-bit IV per encryption and explicit rejection of unknown versions
Recovery key is 128 bits displayed as Crockford base32 and wraps the same `vaultKey` via HKDF info `bw-recovery`
Known-answer tests cover PBKDF2, HKDF, AES-GCM round-trip, tamper rejection, and wrong-password/wrong-recovery-key failures
A benchmark test reports unlock derivation time and fails the budget when exceeded
No secret value appears in console output, thrown error messages, or test snapshots

steps.details: Create `app/lib/crypto/contract.ts` documenting algorithm identifiers, HKDF info strings (`bw-auth`, `bw-wrap`, `bw-recovery`), envelope shape, base64 conventions (URL-safe no padding in transport, standard in storage), and the list of versioned parameters. Export typed constants instead of magic strings.

Create `app/lib/crypto/kdf.ts` with `deriveMasterKey(password, salt, iterations)` using `crypto.subtle.deriveBits` (PBKDF2-SHA256, 32 bytes), `deriveAuthHash(masterKey)` and `deriveWrapKey(masterKey, wrapSalt)` using HKDF-SHA256, and `deriveRecoveryWrapKey(recoverySecret, recoverySalt)`. Normalize passwords with NFKC before derivation and document it, because the format is permanent.

Create `app/lib/crypto/vaultKey.ts` with `generateVaultKey()`, `wrapVaultKey(vaultKey, wrapKey)` returning `{ ct, iv }`, and `unwrapVaultKey({ ct, iv }, wrapKey)`. Reject short or malformed inputs. Never log key material; use typed errors such as `WrongPasswordError` and `MalformedEnvelopeError` with no payload data.

Create `app/lib/crypto/envelope.ts` with `sealItem(plaintextObject, vaultKey)` and `openItem(envelope, vaultKey)`. Serialize plaintext as UTF-8 JSON, encrypt with AES-256-GCM using a fresh random 96-bit IV, and return `{ v: 1, alg: 'A256GCM', iv, ct }` as base64. Validate `v` and `alg` on open and throw `UnsupportedEnvelopeError` for unknown versions.

Create `app/lib/crypto/recovery.ts` with `generateRecoverySecret()` (16 random bytes), `formatRecoveryKey(bytes)` (Crockford base32, 26 chars grouped for display), `parseRecoveryKey(text)` (tolerant of spaces/dashes, rejects invalid checksum characters), and wrap/unwrap helpers that reuse `vaultKey.ts`.

Add tests with fixed vectors for PBKDF2 and HKDF, a round-trip test for seal/open, a test that flips one ciphertext byte and expects failure, a test that reuses an IV and asserts the implementation never does, wrong-password unwrap failure, wrong-recovery-key failure, and an NFKC normalization test (e.g. full-width characters).

Add `app/lib/crypto/__test__/kdf.bench.test.ts` that derives a master key at 600000 iterations and asserts completion under the budget from PRD S2, logging the measured duration. Mark it as a non-flaky benchmark by allowing one retry on shared CI hardware and documenting the threshold.

Create a presentational component that displays the grouped recovery key, requires an explicit stored-it checkbox, and requires typing back a 6-character substring before enabling continue. No server call, no persistence beyond props.

technicalNotes: WebCrypto only; do not add a WASM Argon2 dependency.
HKDF info strings are part of the permanent contract — changing them breaks every stored vault.
Never persist the vault key in localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB plaintext, or React state.
Password normalization must be documented because changing it later locks users out.
This PR contains no routes and no UI beyond the confirmation component.
